title: Consistency of excluded middle and Church’s thesis in Coq
formal:
Is \(\mathcal T+\mathrm{LEM}+\mathrm{CT}\) logically consistent, where \(\mathcal T\) is Coq's ordinary cumulative inductive core calculus specified below, and the two added propositional axioms are
\[\mathrm{LEM}:\quad\forall P:\mathrm{Prop},\ P\lor\neg P,\]
\[\mathrm{CT}:\quad\forall f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N,\ \exists e:\mathbb N,\ \forall x:\mathbb N,\ \exists s:\mathbb N,\ T(e,x,s)=\mathrm{Some}(f(x))?\]
Here \(T\) is the fixed bounded evaluator for ordinary register-machine programs defined below. Consistency means that there is no finite well-typed closed proof term of \(\mathrm{False}\) in the extended calculus. The existence quantifiers in CT are in Prop; they are not computational dependent pairs.
why: This would clarify whether classical reasoning about propositions can coexist with the claim that every internal numerical function is computable, while retaining a rich dependent type theory. The distinction matters for synthetic computability developments that use Church’s thesis as an axiom and for the foundational role of separating propositions from computational data.
status_note: Forster’s Section 7 conjecture, the Coq 8.11 calculus documentation and Putrle’s 2023 consistency theorem were checked on 2026-09-14. The latter explicitly covers a fragment without general inductive types. A bounded later-work search did not identify a consistency model or contradiction for the full ordinary core with exactly the selected two axioms.

sentences: Church’s thesis says that every internal function from natural numbers to natural numbers is computable.
The law of excluded middle gives classical reasoning about propositions.
The question asks whether adding both propositional axioms to Coq’s ordinary cumulative inductive core can produce a contradiction.
The distinction between propositional existence and computable witness extraction is essential.
A 2023 thesis proves consistency for a restricted fragment, leaving the selected full-calculus target beyond that result.

definitions:
The base \(\mathcal T\) is the Prop/Set/Type calculus of inductive constructions in the Coq 8.11 reference manual, with predicative Set and cumulative predicative universes \(\mathrm{Type}_i\) above it. This fixes the source's full inductive-calculus setting rather than only the arithmetic fragment used in some consistency models. The optional separate SProp sort and the impredicative-Set extension are outside this selected core. Terms include variables, universe sorts, dependent products \(\Pi x:A.B(x)\), abstractions, applications, local definitions, inductive constructors, pattern matching and guarded recursive or co-recursive definitions. Definitions and conversion follow the cited calculus: function application reduces by substitution, pattern matching computes on constructors, local definitions unfold, and recursive/co-recursive unfolding obeys the guardedness rules. Universe constraints must have a well-founded assignment to levels. Arbitrary mutual inductive and coinductive declarations satisfying its positivity and universe conditions are permitted; not just a fixed list of natural-number and list types.

Prop is the impredicative universe of propositions: a proposition may quantify over a type at any universe level and remain in Prop. Ordinary data live in Set or Type. Propositional disjunction and existential quantification are inductive propositions. Their proofs generally cannot be pattern-matched to produce arbitrary computational data. The standard exceptions for empty and singleton inductive propositions remain allowed, including elimination of False into any type. Singleton elimination is the calculus's syntactic constructor rule, not a new assumption that every inhabited proposition has one proof. Identity is the usual inductive equality with reflexivity and its permitted elimination rule. Equality reflection, functional or propositional extensionality, univalence, unrestricted choice and proof irrelevance are not added as axioms.

Natural numbers have constructors zero and successor. Fix a computable, effectively decodable Gödel numbering of finite deterministic register-machine programs. Registers hold natural numbers. A program consists of labelled increment-and-jump instructions, decrement-with-zero-test-and-jump instructions, and halt instructions. It starts with register zero containing \(x\), all other registers zero, and its initial program counter at the first instruction; on halting it outputs register zero. The selected model is Turing complete. The total, structurally recursive function \(T(e,x,s)\) simulates the program coded by \(e\) for at most \(s\) transitions, returning \(\mathrm{Some}(y)\) if it has halted with output \(y\), and \(\mathrm{None}\) otherwise. Invalid codes are interpreted as nonhalting programs. The numbering and evaluator are fixed before adding either axiom; CT does not assert the existence of an unspecified oracle evaluator. Standard effectively intertranslatable program codings yield equivalent CT assertions.

The symbol \(\neg P\) means \(P\to\mathrm{False}\), where False is the proposition with no constructors. Add opaque proof constants of the displayed LEM and CT types and no computational reduction equations for them. The quantifier over \(f\) ranges internally over all functions of the extended theory, not merely functions in a chosen list of already written programs. A contradiction would be a closed derivation of False using finitely many permitted declarations and these constants. The question concerns the mathematical inference rules, not bugs in a proof-assistant executable.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof that the extended formal calculus has no closed proof of False, or exhibit such a proof and verify its typing. A semantic construction must include soundness for the selected universes, general permitted inductive/coinductive declarations and elimination rules; modeling only a restricted arithmetic fragment is insufficient. A proof of consistency for CT alone, for a different type theory, or after replacing propositional existentials by a different assertion does not settle this joint-consistency target.

context_blocks.text: Classical set-theoretic reasoning commonly turns an existence statement into a function by choice. Combining such a choice principle with excluded middle produces noncomputable numerical functions and contradicts CT. The source explains that the corresponding choice principle is not derivable merely from Coq’s Prop-level excluded middle.

CT asserts that a program index exists propositionally. It does not provide an operation that extracts an index from an arbitrary function. Likewise, LEM is a propositional disjunction, not a Boolean decision procedure for every proposition. These distinctions are essential to the conjecture.

Forster explicitly conjectures joint consistency at the end of Section 7. Earlier consistency results for Church’s thesis in other constructive type theories do not automatically establish this particular combination of classical logic, impredicative propositions and Coq’s elimination rules.

Putrle’s 2023 thesis proves consistency of the fCIC fragment used for a synthetic computability development, with stronger synthetic computability assumptions and selected large-elimination rules. Its Definition 6.4 and following text explicitly restrict general inductive types. This is substantial partial progress but does not by itself model the full core selected here.
